oracle.method: Closed form of the structural equations, evaluated by plain arithmetic over the sample rows, not by the estimator's design or lag alignment. Law (n = 300, i = 0..n-1): r_i = sin(0.29 i); z_i = 0.4 r_i + cos(0.13 i) + 0.3 sin(1.7 i); t_i = 0.3 + 0.5 r_i + 0.2 z_i + 0.4 cos(2.3 i); y_i = 1 + 2 t_{i-1} + 0.6 z_{i-1} + w_i with w_i = 0.1 sin(0.77 i). Horizon 1, pulse at origin -1: outcome rows s = 1..n-1 with treatment t_{s-1}. Averages over those rows: mean_t, mean_z, mean_w. The z-adjusting completion identifies E[y | do(t@-1 = x)] = 1 + 2 x + 0.6 mean_z + mean_w (a shift by d evaluates x = mean_t + d). The completion that does not adjust for z (z treated as a mediator) identifies the association E[y | t@-1 = x] = mean_y + slope (x - mean_t) with mean_y = 1 + 2 mean_t + 0.6 mean_z + mean_w and slope = 2 + (0.6 cov_tz + cov_tw) / var_t, the omitted-variable-bias formula from the same equations (covariances over the same rows).
oracle.origin_note: hand-derived formulas evaluated with python math (no numpy solver) and cross-checked against a numpy least-squares fit: the z-as-mediator values agree to 1e-15, the z-adjusting completion's fit differs from its structural value by at most 1.1e-3 because the deterministic wiggle w is only asymptotically orthogonal to (t, z)
oracle.formula: adjusting: 1 + 2x + 0.6 mean_z + mean_w; z as mediator: mean_y + slope (x - mean_t), slope = 2 + (0.6 cov_tz + cov_tw)/var_t, over rows s = 1..n-1.

oracle.independence_basis: The generator rebuilds the stated trigonometric law, forms the lag-aligned rows and evaluates the structural level and the omitted-variable slope exactly over rationals; it imports no Antecedent code and no statistics package. The shared object is the stated law and the omitted-variable-bias formula.
